subject: BioFlux discovery: dedicated capacity needs, isolation & SLA next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Elena Grant <elena.grant@bioflux.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2027 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity discovery — isolation, scaling, SLA (BioFlux)

Hi Elena — thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our call plus proposed next steps so we have a single source of truth.

Pain points you called out
- Bursty inference (up to 650 req/s for short periods when research batches run) causing unpredictable latency spikes.
- Multi-tenant safety: you need tenant-level isolation for PHI processing and distinct KMS scopes per customer.
- Cost predictability: procurement needs a predictable committed spend for budget planning.
- Ops readiness: limited internal SRE bandwidth to manage model rollouts and failovers.

Goals we heard
- Production rollout for clinical scoring model (70B transformer) with p50 latency target < 80 ms and p95 < 250 ms.
- Dedicated reserved pool for critical internal workloads + burst policy to handle research spikes.
- SOC2 + evidence for key controls; 3rd-party encryption with customer-managed KMS.

Sizing / initial recommendation (high level)
- Pilot (Q4): reserved pool of 4 x H100-class GPUs (fractional placement if needed) dedicated to BioFlux core cluster with an isolated tenant and separate network path.
- Burst plan: allow cross-pool burst to a shared surge queue up to 2x baseline for 30-minute windows, with automatic fallback to smaller quantized model variant for non-critical traffic.
- Caching: prefix/KV cache for recurrent patient prompts; we estimate 25–35% token reduction for your 60–90s conversation patterns.

SLA targets to discuss with procurement
- Availability: 99.95% for dedicated pool (monthly).
- Latency SLO: p95 under 250 ms on provisioned capacity; staged canary for p50/p95 validation.
- Incident response: 30-minute paging for Sev1; runbook access and biweekly ops sync during onboarding.

Attachments I’m sending with this thread
- isolation-proofing-checklist.xlsx (initial mapping of network/KMS/tenant controls)
- redwood-dedicated-sla-v2.pdf (draft SLA language + uptime targets)
- bioflux-security-questions.xlsx (answers we filled during call; please mark gaps)

Immediate next steps (owner / ETA)
- BioFlux: share procurement cadence and head of security contact (Elena) — by Fri 9/17 (Elena)
- Redwood: produce a 1-page commercial snapshot (pricing ranges for pilot + committed 12-mo path) — by Wed 9/21 (Ben)
- Redwood: technical design diagram showing network isolation and KMS flow for review — by Thu 9/23 (Rishi)
- Joint: 30-minute follow-up with infra/security + procurement (target week of 9/27) — propose slots after we share docs.

If that matches your expectations, I’ll queue the pricing note and Rishi will start the architecture sketch. Happy to jump on another call if you want walk-throughs of the isolation checklist.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Solutions Lead | Redwood Inference

Subject: Cost ranges + technical notes (follow-up)

Hi Elena / team — following up with the two items you asked for on the call: a rough conservative vs aggressive pricing snapshot and a couple technical clarifications for Rishi.

Pricing (pilot monthly run-rate, ballpark)
- Conservative (4 x H100 reserved + limited burst): $125k/month (commit discount applied).
- Aggressive (8 x H100 reserved + generous burst): $210k/month.
Note: these include GPU capacity, orchestration, and 24/7 support but exclude professional services and data egress. We’ll provide a formal commercial one-pager.

Technical clarifications for Rishi / BioFlux infra
- We recommend providing one KMS key per environment (prod/staging) and a separate encryption context per tenant for audit separation.
- Canary rollout: start with a single shard (10–15% traffic) running mixed-precision quantized model; validate p95 before scaling.
- Fallbacks: when surge queue exceeds threshold we will (in order) 1) rate-limit low-priority research traffic, 2) route to quantized variant, 3) if critical, spill to reserved burst pool.
- Observability: we will expose per-tenant token-level cost + latency dashboards; set alerting for p95 breach and token burn rate.

I’ve attached the draft SLA (Marissa included it) and will follow with the commercial snapshot. Rishi — any objections to the KMS / canary plan?

Thanks,
